title: The Three Griefs over the Bound Living Soul
arc: The teaching names three divine powers that proceed from the Father and grieve over the Living Soul caught in the mingled state — the Mother of Life weeping for her captive children, the First Man mourning for his Five Sons standing in danger, and a third grieving power whose description has been broken off — showing that compassion at every level of the Divine accompanies the soul through its tribulation.
reading:
This chapter sets out a brief but precise teaching about compassion as a structural feature of the Divine itself. Three "powers inclined of heart" — three emanations that have come forth from the Father of Greatness — are presented as grieving over the captive light. The teaching is not merely sentimental; it is showing that at the very source of being there is a sorrow that follows the Living Soul into its tribulation. Where the soul suffers in mingled bondage, the Divine in its own emanations suffers correspondingly. This is the spiritual point: the Lord is not indifferent to the soul's mingled state, and the divine accommodation reaches downward as a heart inclined toward what has been bound.

The first who grieves is the Mother of Life — Divine Wisdom in her bringing-forth, the matrix from which spiritual life is generated. She grieves because her children stand in tribulation, mingled with the Darkness and bound up in the entire archonic host. Read correspondentially, these "children" are the truths of life that issued from the maternal pole of divine generation but have fallen into the mingled state of the natural mind. The matrix that gave them birth still feels them; she longs after them as they receive blow after blow within the cosmos. Her grief signifies that the bringing-forth principle of the Divine never abandons what it has generated, even when it is held in foreign bonds. The maternal principle keeps watch over its own light wherever it has been scattered.

The second who grieves is the First Man — Divine Truth descending into the natural to overcome self-love — whose dominion and kingship are established in the Vessel of Light (one of the two ships, sun or moon, the great luminary-vessels by which truth crosses the natural). His grief is for his Five Sons, the five attributes of Divine Truth scattered as the Living Soul into the cosmos, who stand fast in the midst of the danger. The teaching makes a striking move here: every chosen one who is pleasing to the Five — every elect soul whose walking in the regenerate life keeps faith with the dispersed Living Soul — bears upon those Five, so that they not be afflicted further. Conversely, every cry of weeping that rises from a bound soul under the bondages and blows of the Enemy is heard by the First Man, and he answers with grief and mourning. This describes the living conjunction between the elect human and the cosmic Christ-figure of the dispersed Living Soul: the regenerate life relieves the suffering of the divine truth held in matter, and the suffering of any bound soul registers immediately in the heart of the First Man. He continually bears grief on account of his sons.

The third grieving power is named at the close (ⲡⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲉⲧⲣ̄ⲗⲩⲧⲏ) but the text breaks off before its identity and grief are described. By the standard ordering of the emanations and by the logic of "three powers," this third would naturally be the Living Spirit (or, in some orderings, the Third Ambassador) — the operative power that builds order in the receptive natural and continues the work of redemption upon the same captive light over which Mother and First Man already grieve. Whatever the precise figure, the teaching's arc is complete in form: a threefold grief at three discrete levels of the divine economy, corresponding to the matrix that brought the soul forth, the truth that descended after it, and the operative power that works to lift it out. Together they declare that the captivity of the Living Soul is mourned at every register of the Divine, and that this mourning is itself the inward side of redemption — the heart-inclination from which the Call goes forth and the raising is accomplished.
